name: Computer Architecture
blurb: Short videos only: every pick is 20 minutes or less and covers one or two ideas, ordered as a sequence. Most come from IIT Bombay's CS305, Ben Juurlink's Hennessy & Patterson series and David Black-Schaffer's short lectures.
method:
• Length: hard cap of 20 minutes per video; depth comes from a sequence.
  • Order: picks in a subtopic are in watching order; the first is the starting point.
  • Sources: IIT Bombay CS305 (Biswabandan Panda), TU Berlin's Ben Juurlink (follows Hennessy & Patterson), David Black-Schaffer (Uppsala), and animated explainers (BitLemon, Core Dumped) where a picture helps.

subtopics.name: Short-video courses
subtopics.note: Every video on this page is 20 minutes or less, so each subtopic is a sequence of short sittings. These series supply most of them and are worth following in order.

picks.title: CS305@IITB: Computer Architecture

picks.title: Caches by David Black-Schaffer
picks.why: David Black-Schaffer (Uppsala) on caches in 4–12 minute parts. His Virtual Memory series is the companion.

picks.why: Virtual memory from first principles in 14 short videos: page tables, translation, faults, TLBs and multi-level tables.

picks.why: Core Dumped's animated build-up from transistors to a CPU running loops. Good for intuition before the courses.
